solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Influence female luvvie?

parts.note: a luvvie is a gushing theatrical type, i.e. a performer on stage

explanation.surface: A theatrical woman wielding sway over others.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is something that has a bearing on an outcome, a synonym for an influence.

clue.text: Timepiece turned up of black guard

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the little word of is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to keep watch is to guard; a watch is also a guard on duty

explanation.surface: A clock flipped over belonging to a dark-uniformed sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket watch on a chain, worn in a waistcoat, is a kind of timepiece.

clue.text: Acknowledging appearance I run with catcall happily

indicators.note: happily suggests the letters fall out by chance into a fresh order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An actor running on stage to cheers and jeers alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happily' rearranges I, RUN and CATCALL together into the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers return to the stage after the show to bow and acknowledge applause, a fitting description of that final appearance.

clue.text: Miss nothing with German

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A young lady with nothing but a German companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title for a woman, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something out is to leave it out, a synonym.

clue.text: Fleet stacks one in unfortunate fall

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the scrambled letters
unfortunate suggests the word fall has gone awry, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: stacks of something is a lot of it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A navy piling up casualties in an unlucky collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stacks' reads as a verb but is the noun, as in stacks of money; 'unfortunate' scrambles the fall and 'in' places the pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Monarch set aside freedom offering gift

indicators.note: set aside means these letters are put out of the longer word

parts.note: liberation is freedom
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A king abandons liberty while making a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set aside' takes ER out of LIBERATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink poured out as an offering to a god, a gift to the deity.

clue.text: A rift developed about fine cloudy preserve — no-one moves in it

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
developed suggests the words a rift have evolved into a new arrangement

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
c is the weather-map symbol for cloudy
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A crack forms in a jar of murky preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns A RIFT into TRAFI, and 'about' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of a vehicle gridlock: in a traffic jam nobody can move.

clue.text: Top firm thus toppled

indicators.note: toppled means the head of the word is knocked off, so these letters go from its start

parts.note: solid means firm
so means thus

explanation.surface: A leading company brought down in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toppled' knocks SO off the top of SOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is the cover on top of a box or jar, a noun synonym.

clue.text: A run with Rovers' footballer round gully

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Roy of the Rovers is a long-running British comic-strip footballer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dash by a football club's player around a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy of the Rovers was a British comic strip about the footballer Roy Race.
explanation.definitionFit: An arroyo is a steep-sided dry stream bed in arid country, a kind of gully.

clue.text: Chap with attitude

definitions.meaning: a chap is the jaw or side of the face, as in chops

explanation.surface: A bloke full of sass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man, but it is the old word for the jaw or face.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of the face is one sense; the other is impudent talk, which is also called attitude.

clue.text: Buff brand is hot

parts.note: to brand an animal is to burn a mark on it
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A trendy label is fashionable now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' looks like an enthusiast; here it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish metal by rubbing until it shines is to buff it, a synonym.

clue.text: Wild pig facing the German schoolchild

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A wild hog confronting a pupil from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who lives in at a residential school is a boarding pupil.

clue.text: Seafarer's heart is long way away

indicators.note: heart means the central letters of the word Seafarer's are taken

explanation.surface: A sailor's affections are distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle letters of SEAFARER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen from a distance is at a great remove, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Weakness? No, these used to float like a butterfly

definitions.meaning: a hidden flaw in an admired figure

definitions.text: these used to float like a butterfly
definitions.meaning: Cassius Clay, later Muhammad Ali, boasted he would float like a butterfly and sting like a bee

explanation.surface: A boxer's boast about dancing round the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay, so his dancing feet were Clay's.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Daniel's statue in the Bible, means a hidden flaw in someone revered.

clue.text: Potentially are dangling in wheels etc

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Undercarriage parts left hanging loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges ARE DANGLING.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's undercarriage consists of its wheels, struts and associated parts.

clue.text: Sad state to be in, short on gin and bottle?

parts.note: to be low on something is to be short of it
gin is a spirit, and bottle (courage) is spirit too

explanation.surface: A miserable drinker running out of booze and nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a depressed or dejected mood, a sad state.

clue.text: Gorge and get rid of that

parts.note: to can is to discard or sack, as in canning a plan
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Eat greedily and throw that away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like the verb to stuff oneself; it is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, narrow ravine, a synonym of a gorge.

clue.text: Very cool, an active smoker?

indicators.note: active suggests the letters are lively and stirred about into another order

explanation.surface: A trendy person who lights up a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' rearranges COOL AN, and also describes the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano emits smoke and ash, playfully cast as one who smokes.

clue.text: Move disturbing letters by European

indicators.note: disturbing means the word letters is thrown into a different order

explanation.surface: Relocating because of upsetting mail from a continental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate to a new home is to move, a synonym.

clue.text: Without equal — like the House of Commons

definitions.meaning: the Commons has no lords in it, unlike the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Praise for the British lower chamber as unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers sit in the House of Lords, never in the Commons, so the Commons is free of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no match is one sense; the other reads the word as lacking members of the nobility.

clue.text: One of The Wailers outlaws incomplete list

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a ship that lists leans over, or heels

explanation.surface: A reggae band member barred from an unfinished set list.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wailers looks like Bob Marley's band, but it is the wailing spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose wail foretells a death.

clue.text: Superficial dossier about a college

indicators.note: about means the folder goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers

explanation.surface: A shallow report about a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and C inside FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile arguments are glib and lacking depth, a synonym for superficial.

clue.text: Women occupying chairs in "day wear", for some

definitions.note: plural: tracksuit garments, in the plural like the clue

indicators.note: occupying means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: chairs are seats

explanation.surface: Ladies sitting in chairs in casual clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts W inside SEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweatpants and sweatshirts are casual clothing worn all day by some people.

clue.text: Run with every contact

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
each means every

explanation.surface: Jog along with each of your friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone by phone is to get in touch, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gosh! Oil supplier, popular always

parts.note: an oil well supplies crude
in means popular, fashionable
ever means always

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a gusher that never runs dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, interjection synonyms.

clue.text: Backing newspaper about food thickening

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a. is a dictionary abbreviation for about (approximately)

explanation.surface: A tabloid supporting a story on gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns RAG A to read from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a seaweed jelly used to set and thicken desserts and sauces.

clue.text: Modus operandi topped by morning rounds

indicators.note: in a down clue, topped by puts the next piece above the first

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning (ante meridiem)

explanation.surface: A criminal's usual method beginning with dawn gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is supplied as rounds of shot, the informal plural noun.

clue.text: Transport overhead if trial must be shifted

indicators.note: must be shifted means the words if trial are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moving goods by air if the court case is relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be shifted' rearranges IF TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift carries supplies or people by aircraft, through the sky above.

clue.text: Trip breaking urn

indicators.note: breaking suggests the vase is smashed so its letters fall in new order

explanation.surface: Stumbling and smashing a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a stumble; it is a short journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A short journey, such as a quick drive, is a jaunt or trip.

clue.text: MC is brother from Bordeaux on committee

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the piece after the one it follows

parts.note: pere is French for father, used of a priest or religious brother

explanation.surface: A French monk serves as host on a panel.
explanation.walkthrough: Père is strictly French for father; the clue stretches it to a religious brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies introduces acts at a show, which is the host's role.

clue.text: Left base

definitions.meaning: Latin for on the left-hand side, used in heraldry

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for left gave the heraldic left side; it also means menacing or evil.

clue.text: Folk dance in Nottingham or Risley

indicators.note: in signals the letters run within the place names

explanation.surface: Country dancing in two East Midlands places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' shows the answer spans the end of Nottingham, or, and the start of Risley, a Derbyshire village.
explanation.definitionFit: An English folk dance with bells and sticks performed by costumed teams.
